note: Precomputed model outputs, not live generation. Videos contain the shared initial frame followed by every predicted frame, without interpolation. Curated qualitative examples do not replace aggregate test results.
timingNote: A shared initial frame and all future frames are encoded at 4 FPS. 16 s and nominal 4 s prediction horizons produce 16.25 s and 4.25 s media. LuSNAR uses nearest-source sampling; its original nonuniform capture offsets are retained in each sample. MarsLab plays at 1× simulation time: 4 FPS, one shared observed anchor and sixteen future samples over 4 seconds; the final frame is held for 0.25 seconds.

demos.title: Moon 7
demos.model: OpenNWM Nav15 Stage 2, LuSNAR fine-tuned EMA
demos.protocol: Each horizon is predicted from the same four observed context frames and anchor-relative target body pose.
demos.selection: For each held-out Moon_7..9 scene, select the valid 20-frame window with the largest recorded future yaw range (degrees rounded to two decimals, tie: earliest anchor); require at least one meter of traveled future path, unique nearest source frames within 125 ms of the 4 Hz grid, and retain previous evaluation windows plus their 4 s exclusion buffer. Selection uses only recorded ground-truth poses, before new inference; no prediction image or prediction quality is used. Frozen anchors: Moon_7=180, Moon_8=39, Moon_9=713.
limitations: Qualitative ground-truth-curvature-selected held-out scenes; not a random benchmark.
Same original fine-tuned checkpoint; no extra training or test-based checkpoint selection.
Direct predictions share four observed context frames and do not form an autoregressive rollout.
Planar body poses omit height, roll, pitch and camera extrinsics; source capture intervals are nonuniform.
Ground-truth-curvature-selected qualitative examples; not a random benchmark or an accuracy improvement claim. No extra fine-tuning or prediction-based sample selection.

conditioningTrajectory.axes: Forward and left in meters relative to the last observed rover-body pose.
conditioningTrajectory.timeSemantics: Frame 0 is the shared context anchor; frames 1–16 use the paired target pose. Playback is 4 FPS; nonuniform source capture offsets are retained separately.

demos.title: Mars crater · left turn
demos.protocol: Each of sixteen future views is predicted directly from the same four observed RGB frames and its anchor-relative realized PhysX body displacement. The future reference images are not model context. This is action-conditioned direct prediction, not an autoregressive rollout or a navigation success evaluation.
demos.selection: The first 20-frame window of test_00, test_01 and test_02, fixed before training; all six held-out windows are evaluated without ranking predictions. Independent held-out trajectories share the training terrain.
limitations: Independent held-out trajectories share the main_crater terrain; this is not cross-scene generalization.
Actions are realized PhysX body displacements, not a claim that commanded velocity exactly equals traveled motion.
A single translation scale fitted only on training poses is shared by validation and test; metric poses and commands are retained.
The SE(2) action interface discards vertical motion, pitch, and roll.
MarsLab scene and rover assets are run with a minimal Isaac Sim 4.1 recorder, not the complete official Isaac Sim 5.x application.

conditioningTrajectory.axes: Forward and left displacement in meters, relative to the observed anchor.
conditioningTrajectory.timeSemantics: Offsets from synchronized simulator camera/PhysX timestamps; 1× simulation time.
conditioningTrajectory.poseSource: MarsLab / Isaac Sim PhysX body ground truth
